section.t: B"S.
Shabbos Parshas Haazinu,
Shabbos Shuvah 5741*

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the verse "Shuvah Yisrael" and the Alter Rebbe's explanation, raising questions about how teshuvah applies to one on the level of Yisrael.
section.t: "Return, O Yisrael, unto Hashem your G-d, for you have stumbled in your iniquity."
And the Alter Rebbe explained,
that what is written "Return... unto Hashem your G-d"
(even though ostensibly it should have said "to Hashem your G-d")
means,
that the measure of teshuvah is until Hashem becomes your G-d.
And it needs to be understood,
that one who is relevant for
(and is required of him)
such an exalted teshuvah,
is surely a person of an exalted level even before performing this teshuvah,
as is also understood from what is written "Shuvah Yisrael,"
for the name Yisrael is because "you have striven with G-d and with men and have prevailed,"
meaning he is a prince
and rules over the concealment of the name Elokim and over the powers that spread forth from it
and how can the matter of iniquity, which would require teshuvah, apply to him?
And although it is known that teshuvah is not only for transgressions
but rather to return one's soul to its source and root
["and the spirit returns to G-d who gave it"],
for this teshuvah applies even to completely righteous individuals,
nevertheless, the verse explicitly states "Shuvah Yisrael... for you have stumbled in your iniquity,"
and how can the matter of iniquities apply to one who is on this level?
Also, it needs to be understood what the verse continues,
"Take words with you and return to Hashem,"
for after already saying "Shuvah Yisrael," what is added by
("Take words with you")
"and return to Hashem"?
Also, it needs to be understood what it says afterwards,
"Say to Him, 'Forgive all iniquity,'"
for even the saying and request "forgive iniquity" is connected to the matter of teshuvah,
and from this it implies that after the teshuvah of "Shuvah Yisrael" and of "return to Hashem,"
there needs to be yet another teshuvah.
Also, it must be said that in the first teshuvah and in the third teshuvah the matter of iniquity is mentioned
("for you have stumbled in your iniquity,"
"forgive iniquity"),
but not in the second teshuvah.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that there are three levels of teshuvah corresponding to the three verses, based on Likkutei Torah.
section.t: And the point of the explanation regarding this is according to what is explained in Likkutei Torah,
that in teshuvah there are three levels.
Teshuvah of "turn away from evil,"
teshuvah of "and do good,"
and teshuvah of "seek peace," which refers to the Torah, for all who engage in Torah make peace in the heavenly retinue and in the earthly retinue,
and the entire Torah was given to make peace in the world.
And the three teshuvahs in these verses
["Shuvah Yisrael...,"
"and return to Hashem,"
"say to Him, 'Forgive all iniquity'"]
are the three teshuvahs of "turn away from evil," "and do good," and "seek peace."
And this is also why these verses are the beginning of the haftarah of Shabbos Teshuvah,
for on Shabbos Teshuvah all three levels must be present.
And as my father-in-law, the Rebbe, related,
that by the Tzemach Tzedek on Shabbos Teshuvah there were three candles of teshuvah,
and the Tzemach Tzedek said, "There are three teshuvahs,"
and my father-in-law, the Rebbe, explained that they are the three teshuvahs explained in Likkutei Torah.
And this is why in the first teshuvah it is written "Return... for you have stumbled in your iniquity,"
but not in the second teshuvah
("and return to Hashem")
is the matter of iniquity not mentioned,
for the first teshuvah is the teshuvah of "turn away from evil"
("you have stumbled in your iniquity"),
but the second is the teshuvah of "and do good."
And this is also why in the first teshuvah the name Elokim is also mentioned
("unto Hashem your G-d")
and in the second teshuvah only the name Hashem is mentioned
("and return to Hashem")
and in the third teshuvah it is written "say to Him,"
for the teshuvah of "turn away from evil" is that Hashem should be our G-d,
and the teshuvah of "and do good" is to connect and cleave to the name Hashem as He is above the name Elokim,
and the teshuvah of "seek peace" is to cleave and be included in the Atzmus of Ein Sof, which is above the name Hashem.
